claims.text: The starting catalyst is a multi-element alloy with nearly equiatomic principal-element ratios.
The starting catalyst has low platinum-group-metal content.
A 2–3 nm CeO2 overlayer will be deposited on the catalyst by atomic layer deposition.
The ALD treatment will produce a uniform, conformal ceria overlayer.
The ceria overlayer will form a robust interface with the underlying alloy.
The ceria overlayer and alloy interface will enhance oxygen storage.
The ceria overlayer will improve oxygen mobility.
Improved oxygen mobility and storage will facilitate regeneration of active catalytic sites.
The ceria overlayer will protect active sites from deactivation by H2O and NO.
The ceria-alloy interface will retard thermal sintering and aging-related degradation.
The ceria-coated catalyst will retain more catalytic activity than the untreated catalyst during transient, low-temperature operation.
The ceria-coated catalyst will have greater durability than the untreated catalyst after thermal aging.
Adding the ceria overlayer will not increase platinum loading and will preserve low platinum-group-metal consumption.
The untreated catalyst exhibits significant activity loss under thermal aging and exposure to H2O and NO.
The untreated catalyst exhibits durability limitations and may undergo platinum aggregation after thermal aging and exposure to H2O and NO.
An excessively thick or non-uniform ceria coating may obstruct reactant access or create diffusion barriers.
Aging conditions more extreme than typical vehicle operation may overwhelm the protective effect of the ceria coating.
